title.narrative: (SUMS) Stöd för ukrainska mediers överlevnad: Internews 2022-2026
(SUMS) Support for Ukrainian media survival: Internews 2022-2026

description.narrative:
Support for Ukrainian Media Survival (SUMS) is a 36-month 23 MSEK project that will help to ensure the survival of key independent Ukrainian media in the mid-term. The overall objective is: Ukrainian citizens have the reliable information they need to play an active role in the reconstruction and modernisation of their communities.
The overall project objective will be achieved through the following specific objectives:
Specific objective 1: Ensure the financial survival and mid-term sustainability of national, local and hyperlocal media
Specific objective 2: Build local media capacity in gender sensitive reporting and core journalist skills
Specific objective 3: Provide psychosocial support for journalists suffering from trauma and burnout

Support for Ukrainian Media Survival (SUMS) är ett 36-månaders projekt på 23 MSEK som kommer att bidra till att säkerställa överlevnaden för viktiga oberoende ukrainska medier på medellång sikt. Det övergripande målet är att de ukrainska medborgarna ska ha den tillförlitliga information de behöver för att spela en aktiv roll i återuppbyggnaden och moderniseringen av sina samhällen.
Detta övergripande mål kommer att uppnås genom följande särskilda mål:
Mål 1: Säkerställa nationella, lokala och hyperlokala mediers ekonomiska överlevnad och hållbarhet på medellång sikt
Mål 2: Bygga upp lokal mediekapacitet i jämställdhetsmedveten rapportering och grundläggande journalistfärdigheter
Mål 3: Ge psykosocialt stöd till journalister som lider av trauma och utbrändhet.

description.narrative:
Specific objective 1: Ensure the financial survival and mid-term sustainability of national, local and hyperlocal media
SUMS project helped strengthen financial sustainability and audience reach of national level media outlets. Supported media diversified revenue streams and expanded audience engagement, strengthening their ability to operate independently during wartime. For example, New Voice stabilised its subscription model with monthly income reaching up to UAH 1.71 million (~366,300 SEK), while TEXTY expanded its audience by launching a YouTube channel that attracted over 13,000 subscribers and more than 500,000 views, enabling its investigations and analytical reporting to reach new audiences.
Local and hyperlocal media strengthened their editorial and organisational capacity to inform their communities. 30 local media outlets were supported by the project. Local media outlets, supported by partners ABO and Internews Ukraine, were supported by new approaches to content production, and audience engagement. Media teams were able to standardise their work with the Customer Management Service (CMS), Search Engine Optimisation (SEO), advertising, and analytics, but also to adopt new formats from short vertical videos to extensive multimedia stories and solutions journalism.
Apart from classical information role, local media also helped mobilise communities, support civic initiatives, and strengthen social bonds during wartime. For instance, reporting by Hadyach.City increased the adoption of stray animals by 50%. Following an information campaign by FastivNews.City, local community participation in state-funded mammogram screenings increased by 25%. Also, media coverage helped launch a civic initiative to introduce a daily minute of silence in the city of Reni to honour fallen soldiers.
In 2025, thanks to agreement amendment and allocation of additional 10 MSEK, Internews was able to support 17 independent regional media outlets, enabling them to retain staff, strengthen revenue generation, and continue reporting in war-affected communities. By combining emergency assistance with measures to enhance financial resilience, this support helped to ensure the continued operation of trusted local media under challenging conditions. These sub-grants are still ongoing and will conclude in 2026. Some immediate results in 2025 are summarized below:
- Media Na Mezhi achieved strong editorial and content distribution results despite high security challenges in the Sumy border region. The newsroom switched to a digital TV model and launched regular local video news production.
- Hromadske Radio advanced its goal of providing independent information to residents in frontline, border, and temporarily occupied areas. With seven FM transmitters operating across Ukraine, SUMS support ensured continuous broadcasting despite the loss of nine transmitters in the Donetsk and Luhansk regions. Broadcasts remained stable even amidst active shelling in some regions. It was confirmed that Hromadske Radio is accessible in temporary occupied regions.
- Trybuna.Sumy made significant progress in improving its website accessibility and content production and increased its visibility among local audiences. Trybuna.Sumy became the first outlet in the Sumy region to offer full accessibility on web and mobile, setting a regional benchmark for inclusive digital journalism.
- Realna Gazeta strengthened the availability of reliable information about life in the temporary occupied territories of eastern Ukraine and the challenges faced by IDPs. Realna Gazeta remains one of very few outlets covering the life of Ukrainians in the occupied territories. The outlets content and expertise were cited by both Ukrainian and international media, including CBS News.
Specific objective 2: Build local media capacity in gender sensitive reporting and core journalist skills
Volyn Press Club has strengthened gender sensitivity in local media outlets. 5 outlets developed their gender policies from scratch, 5 others strengthened existing ones. In addition, the project also strengthened OSINT and investigative skills among veterans and journalists.
